summary: CEIR-14 sec-40/41 ceir.render: backend-neutral rendering orchestration on RAH's hardened model. A render.scope REGION op (the structured begin/end -- the draws live in its graph region; the crd-ceir-gpu BRIDGE lowers it to the canonical RenderingDesc begin/end + draw verbs the frame graph records today, CEIR-14b; crd-ceir core NEVER links gpu-context -- I3/I4). ATTACHMENTS ARE GENERAL (sec-41): render.color_attachment / render.depth_attachment DECLARE ops each take an image resource + carry per-attachment config (load/store/typed-clear/blend/read-only) and PRODUCE a value of a render-dialect ATTACHMENT TYPE (the 8a Extern type-class machinery; the ROLE -- color vs depth -- rides the TYPE, NOT a string attr, per the 12a one-source-of-truth doctrine). render.scope consumes N of them through its single variadic operand tail. ⛔ the attachment TARGETS are OPERANDS (not attrs) so the 13d per-resource barrier machinery + resource_root normalization SEE them (attribute-encoded targets are invisible to hazard derivation -- the RTT/WAR scar). G-buffer / visibility-buffer / object-ID / primitive-ID / velocity / selection / material-ID are PROGRAM-DEFINED output contracts over general typed attachments -- NOT special ops or canonical fields (sec-41, the RAH-1a.1 lesson lifted to the IR). ⛔ no material/shadow/deferred combinations in op NAMES (sec-40) -- combinations stay typed data/program composition. Effects: render.scope is a CONSERVATIVE baseline (GPUCommand + ambient MemoryReadWrite -- a scope may touch any bound attachment/resource, so it MUST hazard against exports/transfers; 14b narrows to the attachment writes + resource reads in lowering); the attachment-declare ops are EFFECT-FREE metadata (the resource.declare shape). Well-formedness rides the module-walk verifier Context::find_render_misuse (the find_dispatch_misuse house pattern, CEIR-14a): attachment operand is image/view-kinded; render.scope operands are all attachment-typed; at most one depth attachment; draw-family ops (CEIR-14b) are legal ONLY inside a render.scope region; and -- the RAH-1a.1 lesson made STATIC -- a Uint typed-clear only on a uint-format attachment. ⛔ NO-FOLLOW (named, never silently subset): the DRAW FAMILY (draw / indexed / indirect / indirect-count / mesh-dispatch / indirect-mesh / patch-tess) + dynamic state (viewport / scissor / shading-rate) -> CEIR-14b; indirect + indirect-count + mesh/task dispatch (the DrawIndex scar) -> CEIR-14c; RAH-2 resident resource-table binding semantics -> CEIR-14d; multiview / view-selection + fragment-density/foveation + the shading-rate ATTACHMENT -> CEIR-14b dynamic state; mip/layer/aspect attachment VIEWS ride the existing resource.view op (sec-41's typed views); DYNAMIC render area (a runtime viewport) -> CEIR-14b (width/height/sample_count are compile-time scope config here, the RenderingDesc-at-record model).

ops.name: color_attachment
ops.summary: Declare a color attachment over an image (load/store/typed-clear/blend); produces a color-attachment-typed value.
ops.docs: render.color_attachment(%image) {load, store, clear_kind, clear_r/g/b/a | clear_uint, blend} -> %attachment. Declares a color attachment; PRODUCES a color-attachment Extern-typed value (8a; role-in-type). Pure (effect-free metadata -- the resource.declare shape; the read/write hazards ride render.scope + the draws). find_render_misuse: operand(0) image/view-kinded; load/store/clear_kind/blend in their closed vocabularies; clear_kind=uint only on a uint-format attachment (the RAH-1a.1 typed-clear-vs-format check lifted to the IR).

operands.name: image
operands.doc: the color target image (or a resource.view subresource of one); its CEIR-3c type is the attachment's underlying format

results.name: attachment
results.doc: the color-attachment value (an 8a Extern type of the render.color_attachment class, wrapping the image type); consumed by render.scope's variadic tail

attributes.name: load
attributes.doc: sec-41 the LoadOp: clear | load | dontcare (absent = clear). CLOSED vocabulary, find_render_misuse enforces it.

attributes.name: store
attributes.doc: sec-41 the StoreOp: store | dontcare (absent = store). CLOSED vocabulary, enforced.

attributes.name: clear_kind
attributes.doc: the typed-clear selector: float | uint (absent = float). CLOSED. `float` reads clear_r..clear_a; `uint` reads clear_uint (RAH-1a.1 -- a uint/id target). find_render_misuse: `uint` only on a uint-format attachment.

attributes.name: clear_r
attributes.doc: float clear red (clear_kind=float; absent = 0.0)

attributes.name: clear_g
attributes.doc: float clear green (absent = 0.0)

attributes.name: clear_b
attributes.doc: float clear blue (absent = 0.0)

attributes.name: clear_a
attributes.doc: float clear alpha (absent = 0.0)

attributes.name: clear_uint
attributes.doc: uint clear id (clear_kind=uint; the R32_UINT background id -- RAH-1a.1 clear_uint; absent = 0)

attributes.name: blend
attributes.doc: sec-40 the per-attachment BlendMode: opaque | alpha | additive | premultiplied | multiply | revealage_multiply | reveal_composite (absent = opaque). CLOSED vocabulary, enforced. The last three are the WBOIT MRT modes (CEIR-16d-live-4a: revealage_multiply is dst*(1-src.rgb), which no generic mode expresses). (The blend STATE surface beyond these presets is CEIR-14b pipeline state.)

ops.name: depth_attachment
ops.summary: Declare the depth/stencil attachment over an image (load/store/clear/compare/read-only); produces a depth-attachment-typed value.
ops.docs: render.depth_attachment(%image) {load, store, clear_depth, compare, read_only} -> %attachment. Declares the depth/stencil attachment; PRODUCES a depth-attachment Extern-typed value. Pure (effect-free metadata). find_render_misuse: operand(0) image/view-kinded (a depth/stencil format); load/store/compare in their closed vocabularies; at most ONE depth_attachment per render.scope. Separate stencil load/store + the stencil aspect is named-forward (CEIR-14b+).

operands.name: image
operands.doc: the depth/stencil target image (or a resource.view subresource); its CEIR-3c type is the underlying depth/stencil format

results.name: attachment
results.doc: the depth-attachment value (an 8a Extern type of the render.depth_attachment class); consumed by render.scope's variadic tail (at most one per scope)

attributes.name: load
attributes.doc: sec-41 the depth LoadOp: clear | load | dontcare (absent = clear). CLOSED, enforced.

attributes.name: store
attributes.doc: sec-41 the depth StoreOp: store | dontcare (absent = store). CLOSED, enforced.

attributes.name: clear_depth
attributes.doc: the normalized device depth clear [0,1] (absent = 1.0 -- the RAH DepthStencilAttachmentDesc default). A raw NDC scalar.

attributes.name: compare
attributes.doc: the DepthCompare: never | less | equal | less_equal | greater | not_equal | greater_equal | always (absent = less_equal). CLOSED vocabulary, enforced.

attributes.name: read_only
attributes.doc: sec-41 READ-ONLY depth/stencil (absent = false). A RO-depth attachment (a depth-prepass reuse / shadow read) -- the FS may sample it but not write. find_render_misuse pairs it with the draws' depth-write state at 14b.

ops.name: draw
ops.summary: A non-indexed draw: run @program over vertex_count x instance_count with the bound resources (inside a render.scope).
ops.docs: render.draw(%vertex_count, %instance_count, %bindings...) {program=@p, access="...", first_vertex=F, geometry=procedural|pull}. A non-indexed draw (StoragePull/None geometry), RESULTLESS, legal ONLY inside a render.scope region. Effects: GPUCommand + a CONSERVATIVE ambient MemoryReadWrite (two blended draws to one attachment must not reorder -- pairwise hazards pin raster order). The geometry mode is program semantics: absent it is INFERRED from binding presence, but `geometry` pins it explicitly for the procedural-with-bindings edge (a texture-reading fullscreen is procedural, CEIR-16-3b-1b). CEIR-13c [op.kernel_ref] {program, program_interface}. find_render_misuse: counts (operands 0-1) Index-typed (DrawCountNotIndex); program a Symbol (ProgramNotSymbol); access-token-count == num_operands-2; each binding (operands 2..) resource-kinded.

operands.name: vertex_count
operands.doc: the vertex count (a runtime index; a compile-time count is an arith.const operand -- const-folded in lowering, a dynamic count -> UnsupportedCommand)

operands.name: instance_count
operands.doc: the instance count (a runtime index; callers pass arith.const 1 for a single instance)

operands.name: bindings
operands.doc: the draw's bound resources (vertex-pull storage buffers, textures, ...), in SLOT order; each binding's ACCESS is the matching `access` token, its KIND derives from its CEIR-3c type

attributes.name: program
attributes.doc: the graphics program/pipeline asset identity (@program); CEIR-13c: extracted as a ckir_ref + resolved/pin-checked by the cook's resolver. ⛔ identity is LOAD-BEARING: an absent/non-symbol program is ProgramNotSymbol (find_render_misuse).

attributes.name: access
attributes.doc: per-binding access: comma-separated {r|w|rw} in binding operand order, one token per binding (empty string = zero bindings). find_render_misuse checks token-count == num bindings and each token in {r,w,rw}.

attributes.name: program_interface
attributes.doc: CEIR-13c the EXPECTED §107 interface hash of @program (a PIN, the u64 stored as its i64 bit pattern; absent = unpinned). Checked vs the resolved program at cook.

attributes.name: first_vertex
attributes.doc: sec-40 the START vertex (absent = 0; the GeometrySource.first_vertex u32 field). A static ATTR (compile-time).

attributes.name: geometry
attributes.doc: CEIR-16-3b-1b the GEOMETRY-SOURCE mode: procedural | pull (absent = INFERRED -- 0 bindings => procedural/None, >=1 => pull/StoragePull, the 14b heuristic). EXPLICIT for the procedural-with-bindings edge: a FULLSCREEN composite reads TEXTURES yet sources vertices procedurally (the VS reads gl_VertexIndex), so it is `procedural` DESPITE its bindings -- without this it infers StoragePull and, with no vertex buffer bound, the encoder's StoragePull arm draws NOTHING (a black pass). CLOSED {procedural, pull}.

ops.name: draw_indexed
ops.summary: An indexed draw: run @program over index_count indices (bound index buffer) x instance_count with the bound resources.
ops.docs: render.draw_indexed(%index_count, %instance_count, %index_buffer, %bindings...) {program=@p, access="...", first_index=F}. An indexed draw, RESULTLESS, legal ONLY inside a render.scope region. Effects: GPUCommand + ambient MemoryReadWrite + a static MemoryRead on %index_buffer (operand 2). CEIR-13c [op.kernel_ref] {program, program_interface}. find_render_misuse: counts (operands 0-1) Index-typed; index_buffer (operand 2) a Buffer/View-of-buffer; program a Symbol; access-token-count == num_operands-3; each binding (operands 3..) resource-kinded.

operands.name: instance_count
operands.doc: the instance count (a runtime index)

operands.name: index_buffer
operands.doc: the index buffer (a Buffer or a View of one -- read GPU-side; carries a static MemoryRead)

operands.doc: the draw's bound resources, in SLOT order (as render.draw)

attributes.doc: per-binding access over the variadic bindings tail: comma-separated {r|w|rw}, one token per binding (empty = zero bindings)

attributes.name: first_index

ops.name: draw_indirect
ops.summary: An indirect draw: @program with draw params read from an %args buffer, up to max_draws sub-draws, inside a render.scope.
ops.docs: render.draw_indirect(%args, %bindings...) {program=@p, access="...", max_draws=N, args_offset=O}. An indirect draw (GeometryKind::Indirect), RESULTLESS, legal ONLY inside a render.scope region. Effects: GPUCommand + ambient MemoryReadWrite + a static MemoryRead on %args (operand 0). ⭐ max_draws = the DrawIndex range (14z pushes the row; REN-40). find_render_misuse: args (operand 0) a Buffer/View-of-buffer (IndirectArgsNotBuffer); program a Symbol; max_draws >=1; access-token-count == num_operands-1; bindings (operands 1..) resource-kinded.

attributes.name: max_draws

Effects: GPUCommand + ambient MemoryReadWrite + a static MemoryRead on %args (0) AND %count (1). find_render_misuse: args (0) + count (1) each a Buffer/View-of-buffer (IndirectArgsNotBuffer / IndirectCountNotBuffer); program a Symbol; max_draws >=1; access arity == num_operands-2; bindings (operands 2..) resource-kinded.

ops.name: scene_draw_list
ops.summary: The scene per-draw-item verb ladder: ONE render.scope, N packets over the host DrawList; each item's fields (args/index_count/texture/storage) select its verb (indirect/indexed/storage-pull/coalesced-multi).
ops.docs: render.scene_draw_list() {program=@p, access="", geometry?}. The scene per-draw-item verb ladder: ONE render.scope, the walk expands it over the host DrawList (ctx.draws()) into N raster packets. In the default `storage` mode the verb is chosen PER ITEM (DrawIndexedIndirect | DrawIndexed | Draw StoragePull | DrawMulti/DrawMultiIndexed run-coalesced); in `procedural` mode (the §41 visbuffer form) each item is a plain procedural Draw (GeometryKind::None, vertex_count, no storage/textures/coalescing). RESULTLESS, legal ONLY inside a render.scope. Effects: GPUCommand + ambient MemoryReadWrite. find_render_misuse: ZERO operands (access arity 0); program a Symbol; geometry in {storage, procedural}.

attributes.doc: CEIR-13c the EXPECTED §107 interface hash (a PIN; absent = unpinned)

attributes.doc: CEIR-16z the geometry mode: storage | procedural (absent = storage). CLOSED vocabulary, find_render_misuse enforces it. `storage` = the ordinary storage-pull scene ladder; `procedural` = a visbuffer / gl_VertexIndex draw (GeometryKind::None, vertex_count only, NO storage binding, no textures, no coalescing) — the §41 visbuffer dissolution onto scene.raster.

ops.name: scope
ops.summary: A render scope: bind the attachments + render area, run the draws in the region. Lowers to RenderingDesc begin/end + draw verbs (14b).
ops.docs: render.scope(%attachments...) {width, height, sample_count, extent_from_target} { ...draws (14b)... }. A render scope, RESULTLESS, carrying a graph region for the draws. Effects: GPUCommand + a CONSERVATIVE ambient MemoryReadWrite (14b narrows to the attachment writes + resource reads in lowering). `extent_from_target` (CEIR-16-3c) makes the render area the RESOLVED colour target size at record (the fullscreen-composite case), the static width/height then a placeholder. find_render_misuse: every operand attachment-typed (a render.color_attachment / render.depth_attachment result); at most ONE depth attachment; width/height >= 1; sample_count a power of two in [1,64]; the region holds only render draw-family ops (14b) + structured control flow.

operands.name: attachments
operands.doc: the color + depth attachments (from render.color_attachment / render.depth_attachment), in SLOT order -> the color[] array order; the depth attachment is recognized by its TYPE. Zero attachments is legal (a no-op scope / a pure-compute-in-a-render-pass is 14b+).

attributes.name: width
attributes.doc: the render-area width in pixels (>=1). Compile-time scope config (the RenderingDesc-at-record model); a DYNAMIC viewport is CEIR-14b dynamic state. find_render_misuse: >=1.

attributes.name: height
attributes.doc: the render-area height in pixels (>=1). find_render_misuse: >=1.

attributes.name: sample_count
attributes.doc: MSAA sample count (absent = 1; >1 => multisample + resolve, sec-41). find_render_misuse: a power of two in [1,64].

attributes.name: extent_from_target
attributes.doc: CEIR-16-3c the render area is the RESOLVED colour target's size at record (absent = false = the static width/height above). A FULLSCREEN composite renders to whatever target it is bound to -- a per-cascade shadow atlas, a half-res buffer, the swapchain -- whose size is only known at record; the authored `width`/`height` stay a valid >=1 placeholder (find_render_misuse unchanged) but are IGNORED, and the materializer reads color[0]->width()/height() instead. ⛔ requires >=1 colour attachment.
